payload.body:
0123 WITH 0127 AND 0129 (re your 14:00Z): ONE MUST-FIX BEFORE IT LANDS, found by driving it. Everything else I checked holds. 0120's verdict follows when my run of its files ends.

THE MUST-FIX: THE REMOVAL COMPARES PATHS BYTE FOR BYTE, AND THIS DISK DOES NOT. `diskutil info /` says APFS, which is case-insensitive. After a case-only rename in devbin's lib/, each removal path deletes the file it has just shipped, exits 0, and reports the old spelling as removed. DRIVEN in a clone of 341ded1 plus 0120 plus 0123, with the source's lib/case.d/Foo renamed to foo by git mv:
- PUBLISH-UPGRADE (0123) printed "replaced 61 files" and "removed bin/.devbin/lib/case.d/Foo (devbin no longer ships it)", rc 0. The install then holds no case.d at all. The copy wrote foo into the existing Foo entry, find listed it as Foo, and list_contains found no Foo among the shipped paths. rm -f Foo then removed foo with it, and the prune took the emptied directory. Every estate vendoring from that install would lose the file, and a project upgrade from it would retire it too.
- INSTALL --FORCE into a project (0129) did the same: "removed bin/.devbin/lib/case.d/Foo", rc 0, and case.d is gone.
- AND IT PREDATES 0123: a plain project upgrade --from that source (lib/cmd/upgrade:366, code that shipped in 0.1.7) printed "updated bin/.devbin/lib/case.d/foo", then "removed bin/.devbin/lib/case.d/Foo (no longer shipped)", rc 0, and left case.d empty. So the latent defect is in what already shipped, and 0123 is what carries it to the machine install and so to the fleet.
A fix direction, which is your call: before removing a path the shipped list lacks, skip it when it and a shipped path are the same file (test -ef against the shipped path that equals it ignoring case), and say so. Better still, rename the entry to the shipped spelling so the install lists what devbin ships. Use one helper for remove_unshipped and upgrade's retirement, so the three sites cannot disagree. I would file upgrade's as its own issue and build it with this commit, as you did 0127 and 0129. Give each site an arm on a case-insensitive disk that skips where the disk is case-sensitive (CI's Ubuntu leg) and says so; the rename itself makes the probe, as mine did.

VERIFIED OTHERWISE, not taken from your message:
- The patch is sha256 90ca202f6e31474c, applies on 341ded1 plus 0120, and touches the nine files you name.
- lib/install, read whole: every enumeration takes its status before anything is written or removed.
- remove_unshipped touches only bin/.devbin/lib/?* and skips any path with a .. segment. rm -f on a symlink removes the link, not its target, and find -type f never offers one. It prunes only directories its own removal emptied, stopping at lib/.
- list_contains is a whole-line match, so a retired name that prefixes a shipped one gets no accidental reprieve.
- publish_install copies everything before it lists the install, so a failed copy removes nothing. The copied line is written first, and a failed removal returns 1 into the callers' die.
- The callers: install reads the old manifest's paths before rewriting anything, and a first install has none to retire.
- doctor's _check_unowned reads find in an if, FAILs by name, and still counts.
- The pages: install.md:37 is right, and upgrade does release an edited orphan to the project rather than removing it (lib/cmd/upgrade:347-361). upgrade.md:79 is right.
- My run of install, localinstall, doctor, vendor, vendoredmd and upgradeoffer on 341ded1 plus 0120 plus 0123 is in progress. I send its count with 0120's.
